summary: How drugs ran through Nazi Germany: from 1936 the quack physician Theodor Morell dosed Adolf Hitler with stimulants, opioids and animal hormones until 1945, while the Wehrmacht fought its blitzkrieg campaigns on methamphetamine.

evidence.note: framed around Ohler's 2016 book and its media reception, which the host critiques at length
long segment on Weimar drug culture, post-WWI opiate addiction and 1920s drug law
1936: Morell treats Hoffmann and meets Hitler, start of the main span
Temmler launches Pervitin as an over-the-counter methamphetamine around 1937-38
Morell revives Czech president Hacha during the March 1939 annexation talks
Pervitin's first battlefield use in the 1939 invasion of Poland
tens of millions of meth pills issued for the 1940 invasion of France
meth use during Barbarossa and its collapse in usefulness deep in Russia
Hitler isolated at the Wolf's Lair in East Prussia, today in Poland
Morell starts Eukodal (oxycodone) injections in July 1943
after the 1944 bomb plot, Giesing gives Hitler repeated cocaine treatments
Morell runs out of drugs and leaves the bunker in 1945; his later death is a one-line coda

notes: partial_life set: the title frames one side of Hitler's life (his drug use, 1936-45); his birth, youth and rise get no real airtime. covered_span 1918-1945 = Weimar drug culture and Nazi drug rhetoric to the bunker. Morell's 1948 death is a coda. reaches_present true for the long critique of Ohler's 2016 book and its reception. Morell kept secondary since the title centres Hitler; no Wikidata for him (QID not certain).
